questions.q: How did tin buttons contribute to Napoleon's Russian defeat?
a: Tin crumbles in extreme cold, ruining the soldiers' clothing
Tin attracted enemy fire and revealed positions
Tin was too heavy for soldiers to march in
Tin melted in rain and stained their uniforms
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the French wore tin, which degrades in low temperatures, leaving soldiers with the tin disease.

questions.q: How did Manhattan change hands, according to the summary?
a: It was traded for Run, an island rich in nutmeg
It was captured in a naval battle with Spain
It was bought from France for a small sum
It was granted as a wedding dowry
questions.why: Lesson 1 says New Amsterdam was given to the English in exchange for Run, where nutmeg was plentiful.

questions.q: How did William Perkin's purple dye come about?
a: He was trying to create a cure for malaria
He was testing a new soap formula
He was dyeing cloth for Queen Victoria
He was refining a medicine for fever
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Perkin discovered the synthetic dye while attempting to make a malaria cure.

questions.q: How did penicillin come to be discovered?
a: A failed experiment led to the discovery
A doctor searched for it deliberately for years
A patient's blood sample revealed it
A dye manufacturer stumbled on it
questions.why: Lesson 2 presents Fleming's penicillin as a failed experiment that accidentally produced a vital medicine.

questions.q: What does the summary say about science and religion?
a: Religion long led, but science is proving powerful too
Science and religion have always stayed separate
Religion explains chemistry better than science
Science has replaced religion in most societies
questions.why: Lesson 3 says religion has traditionally driven the world, while science is quickly showing its own power.
